assertion.objects: The p-adic Tate representation of an elliptic curve over Q.
assertion.hypotheses: For the open SL2 image assertion the elliptic curve is non-CM.
assertion.quantifiers: Every datum meeting the stated hypotheses.
assertion.parameter_range: All primes p, including2; the theorem below is restricted to height-one primes not containing p.
assertion.uniformity: Exact localized module assertions, not a uniform bound in the size of an auxiliary group.
assertion.normalizations: Condition0.6(iii) concerns roots of P_l(t), hence weight minus one for the Tate representation.
assertion.exceptional_cases: No assertion here uses the stronger residual hypotheses required at primes containing p.
assertion.limit_order: The p-adic Tate representation; no additional limit interchange.
assertion.statement: Apply the elliptic statement to the original non-CM curve, then its quadratic twist. The character is trivial on G_(Qab), so the same open SL2 subgroup and unipotent act on V tensor chi; both real eigenspaces have rank one. Upper and lower unipotents also give absolute irreducibility on the cyclotomic subgroup.

cj_original.argument: The fixed-type lattice construction provides an actual labelled CM elliptic curve and cyclic level subgroup. Integral j and common good reduction give its special curve; forward inert reduction makes it supersingular and injectivity of the O action embeds F in its endomorphism algebra B. Ribet realizes its enhanced pair in the stated adelic class set. This independently supplies the reference object and permits choosing i from it. For other local tuples, the actual local lattice classification and labelled conjugacy give z0, and the geometric class-set realization supplies its underlying pair. This does not use the later reduction-torsor bijection to manufacture the reference object.

cj_original.argument: The accepted global quotient/dual-subgroup proof identifies the actual W_(p^e) at CJ66 with the local integral-projector swap, including p=2, preserving the q orientation. The split-support calculation makes the selected root reverse, so the actual root character contributes alpha_p(-1)=w_(p^e)chi_hstar(p)^e. The same actual eigenquotient has pi(Wx)=[w]pi(x)+pi(W infinity); fixed L kills the separately supplied cuspidal translation. Reduced norm valuation e then makes its norm-weighted value change by the same sign. At q, the accepted division model conjugates the nonzero trace-zero residue to its negative, giving (-1/q)=-1, while the unramified norm character contributes chi_hstar(q)=-1. Ribet identifies the operation with Frobenius on coarse points, and the actual additive lambda has sign +1. Multiplying these separate factors gives equal contributions; the prior stabilizer count supplies the multiplicity, not these signs.

cj_original.argument: The fixed negative odd fundamental hstar splits at2N; admissible D is positive squarefree, prime to the fixed support and in the prescribed unit-squareclasses. Thus Dhstar is odd squarefree and1mod4, and locally differs from hstar by a square at2N; it is a negative fundamental discriminant and the resulting field splits there. Splitting at2 excludes the only imaginary quadratic extra-unit fields Q(i) and Q(sqrt(-3)). At the actual nonzero coefficient support, the division residue is nonzero and its square is a nonsquare at q, so q is unramified inert in Q(sqrt(Dhstar)); this is a support condition on D, not a claim that every unrestricted D works at every detector. The actual detector separately supplies (hstar/q)=-1, q outside all fixed support, and the additive lambda:E(F_(q^2))->Z/2^M with Frobenius sign+1. These are the same lambda and fixed L used in the unaveraged sum at79.

Conductor one and maximal O only; no nonmaximal-order or conductor-changing assertion.
